newsitem.title: INDIA: DE BEERS SEEKS TO SET UP INDIA UNIT-PAPER.
newsitem.headline: DE BEERS SEEKS TO SET UP INDIA UNIT-PAPER.

text.p: South African mining giant De Beers has applied to the Indian government for permission to set up a 100 percent-owned subsidiary, Business Standard said on Tuesday.
The daily said the move was in addition to a joint venture it had set up in equal partnership with India's Reliance Industries Ltd, called Diamond Prospecting Private Ltd.
"At the moment we are not sure what kind of entity, in terms of equity holding, the government will approve of in diamond prospecting and mining," the newspaper quoted a De Beers executive as saying.

"So while we already have a joint venture with an Indian partner, we are also setting up a 100 percent subsidiary to make sure that we can participate in the tender process in whatever form the government decides," he said.

A senior government official in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh told Reuters last month that De Beers had decided against bidding for mining rights in the province after the government refused to sell diamonds mined in the state through the firm's Central Selling Organisation (CSO).

The government of the state, India's main diamond mining centre, in January backtracked on a decision to award De Beers a lease to mine diamonds in the state and said it would float fresh tenders for diamond prospecting later in the year.
